label: accepted

evidence.V1: Stacked-tier conifer silhouette with scalloped tier edges reads instantly from front, three-quarter and top (star-shaped plan); strong at 64 px.
evidence.V2: Clear big (4 tiers decreasing upward), medium (light rim band under each tier) and small (pointed tip cap, scallops) hierarchy.
evidence.V3: Stylised tiered cones are confident, but the trunk is reduced to a tiny brown disc under the bottom tier so the tree looks like it sits on its skirt; proportion only partly right.
evidence.V4: Consistent rounded bevel on every tier rim and the tip, catching light as a lighter band; no razor edges.
evidence.V5: Tier faces and rims shade cleanly in studio and flat close-ups; only gentle radial facets on the cones, no pinches or z-fighting. (Trunk-base close-up camera sits inside the foliage and shows only green, so the trunk itself is unverified there.)
evidence.V6: One foliage hue in two values (body + lighter rim) plus a sliver of bark brown; colourways (autumn, frost) keep the same disciplined two-value scheme.
evidence.V7: 1920 tris vs tree target 2000 (ceiling 5000): at target.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material, smooth weighted shading, consistent bevels and a value-banded palette: matches the kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre: correct.

evidence.V1: Four stacked wavy-rimmed tiers with a pointed tip read instantly as a pine from front, three-quarter and silhouette; top view is a clear layered star.
evidence.V2: Big cone mass and medium tiers with light rim bands are clear, but there is no small tier: the trunk is a barely visible stub under the bottom skirt and there are no cones, branches or tufts.
evidence.V3: Tapering tiers with scalloped drooping rims give a confident, toy-like stylised pine; tier spacing and taper are well judged.
evidence.V4: Every tier rim carries a consistent lighter chamfer band that catches light evenly, and the tip has a matching cap band.
evidence.V5: Tier-rim and tip close-ups are clean smooth shells with no pinches, seams or z-fighting; 0 cross-shell overlaps, A17/A18 pass. (Trunk-base close-up camera lands inside the foliage, so it shows nothing.)
evidence.V6: One foliage hue in 2 values (body + rim) with a small bark-brown secondary; autumn and frost colourways keep the same discipline.
evidence.V7: 1920 tris vs tree target 2000 - at/under target.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, smooth fused shells with chamfered rim bands and foliage + bark palette as the Nature spec describes.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre.

evidence.V1: Classic stacked-tier conifer reads instantly from front, 3/4 and silhouette (stepped triangle with wavy tier rims); top view shows concentric star-shaped tiers around the tip.
evidence.V2: Big tiered cone and small rim bands/tip cap read, but the medium trunk tier is effectively missing: only a thin brown disc shows under the bottom tier, and the trunk-base close-up shows nothing but green underside.
evidence.V3: Tier proportions taper nicely, but each tier is a plain cone with a scalloped rim and the tree sits on the ground with no visible trunk, giving a stiff, primitive cone-stack feel.
evidence.V4: Every tier ends in a consistent thick lighter-green lip with a soft chamfer that catches light (tier-rim close-up), tip has the same capped treatment.
evidence.V5: Clean smooth shading on tiers and rims in studio and flat close-ups; no pinches, seams or z-fighting (0 cross-shell overlaps).
evidence.V6: Foliage green in two values (body + light rim) and a bark brown; autumn (with gold rims) and frost colourways stay disciplined.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material, smooth fused shells, foliage hue + bark secondary; fits the nature kit.
evidence.V9: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, SmoothPlastic, MeshPart.Color white, origin bottom-centre.

artifacts: Trunk-base close-up camera is inside the canopy (frame is solid green)
Trunk barely visible below the lowest tier
top_fixes: Lengthen/expose the trunk (about 0.6-1 stud visible below the bottom tier, slight root flare) so the tree does not read as sitting on its skirt
Fix the trunk_base close-up camera so it frames the trunk
Optionally add a slight random twist/offset per tier for a less mechanical stack
Lengthen the exposed trunk so a bark section shows below the bottom tier (fixes the small tier and the trunk-base close-up)
Add a small detail tier: a couple of cones or a tilted tip tuft
Vary tier rotation/scallop slightly so the cone reads less like a perfect stack of primitives
Expose a short tapered trunk (0.6-1 stud) with a small root flare below the bottom tier so the tree is not a cone sitting on the ground
Add slight droop/tilt variation or offset between tiers so the stack reads less like identical primitive cones
Vary rim scallop depth per tier for more organic hierarchy
